newsitem.title: FRANCE: NATO summit spares Chirac feelings.
newsitem.headline: NATO summit spares Chirac feelings.

text.p: No one mentioned France's general election, which went disastrously wrong for President Jacques Chirac, when he played host to world leaders at a Paris summit to mark the signing of a NATO-Russia pact, a participant said on Tuesday.

"There was very little discussion on that (the election) because it's still fresh in Mr Chirac's mind and I think he was enjoying himself so much that we didn't want to raise the topic," said Canadian Minister for Indian Affairs Ronald Irwin.
Answering reporters' questions about the topics discussed on the sidelines of the summit, Irwin said: "It's no secret that Mr Chirac has had a very difficult election."

The conservative French president called the May 25-June 1 vote to assure himself of a friendly parliamentary majority for the rest of his term until 2002, but Sunday's first round saw his centre-right coalition drubbed by the left-wing opposition.
Irwin represented Canada at the summit because Prime Minister Jean Chretien had to stay at home to campaign for re-election in next Monday's Canadian general election.
